## 6. Recommended Technology Stack & Build-vs-Buy Guidance

Real options with trade-offs; the team retains judgment.

**TTS (build-on-open or buy):**
- *Open:* **Piper** (natural, efficient, good for on-device/low-resource), **Coqui XTTS v2** (multilingual, future uncertain since Coqui's backer wound down), **eSpeak-NG** (robotic but tiny and huge language coverage — good last-resort fallback), **Meta MMS-TTS** (1,100+ languages but with notable gaps, e.g., excludes Pashto).
- *Buy:* **Azure Neural TTS** (broad coverage incl. some low-resource locales — e.g., the only verified commercial Pashto voices in one 2026 study), Google Cloud TTS, Amazon Polly.
- *Guidance:* multi-engine abstraction; pick per-language by quality; fall back to eSpeak-NG for unsupported languages rather than failing.

**ASR (build-on-open or buy):**
- *Open:* **OpenAI Whisper** (trained on 680k hrs, ~100 languages, robust; large models need 8GB+ VRAM), **Vosk**/**Kaldi** (streaming/live), **NVIDIA NeMo**; SSL backbones (wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, WavLM, XLS-R) for fine-tuning low-resource languages.
- *Buy:* Google STT (low latency), Azure.
- *Guidance:* run **language ID before ASR**; fine-tune Whisper for priority low-resource languages (documented WER gains, e.g., Welsh 31.86%→18.06% after LoRA fine-tuning); never assume English.

**Real-time audio infrastructure (buy-managed then self-host):**
- **LiveKit** (open-source, Apache-2.0, Go, SFU; SDKs across 11 frameworks; Agents framework for AI participants; DTLS-SRTP by default with optional E2EE via WebRTC Insertable Streams). *Alternatives:* **mediasoup** (mature, flexible), **Janus** (battle-tested, SIP gateway plugin for PSTN bridging), managed **Agora/Daily/Twilio/Amazon Chime**.
- *Architecture:* **SFU** for group rooms (forwards without re-encoding; scales; separate small publisher set from large listener set); P2P only for 1:1 (P2P scales O(N²), breaks down above ~4 participants); MCU only to bridge PSTN/legacy SIP. Use **simulcast** for heterogeneous networks.
- *Guidance:* start on managed (LiveKit Cloud) for MVP; self-host when scale/cost/data-sovereignty demand it. Note: E2EE (Insertable Streams) precludes server-side recording/AI on that stream.

**Telephony / Global South (buy aggregator + open telephony):**
- **Africa's Talking** (USSD/Voice/SMS/Airtime across multiple African markets, free sandbox, `CON`/`END` USSD semantics); **Twilio**/**Vonage** for global voice/SMS; **WhatsApp Business API**.
- *Open telephony:* **Asterisk** / **FreeSWITCH** for self-hosted IVR.
- *Codec:* **Opus** (mandatory in WebRTC; 6–510 kbps; SILK+CELT; DTX + FEC; voip mode ~16–32 kbps for voice).

**AI / VLM (buy API + on-device):**
- *Cloud VLMs:* GPT-class, Claude, Gemini. Per-image token mechanics differ sharply — Gemini uses a flat ~258 tokens/image regardless of resolution (cheapest for high-res); OpenAI tiles at ~170 tokens/512px tile + 85 base (~765 tokens for 1024²); Anthropic ~1,380 tokens/megapixel (~1,334 for 1024², most expensive per image). An independent 2026 comparison spanned ~13× per-image cost (Qwen VL Max $0.0003 → Claude $0.0040) with ~1.2–2.5s/image latency. Cloud accuracy is higher but adds latency, per-image cost, and sends user images off-device.
- *On-device VLMs:* **Apple Foundation Models** framework (on-device ~3B model, image input on newer OS; no per-token cost, offline, private), **Google Gemini Nano** (~3.25B), **Llama 3.2 Vision** (11B/90B), **Moondream 2** (~2B; runs <4GB VRAM; captioning/VQA/OCR), **Qwen-VL** (3B–72B). On-device trades some accuracy for privacy/latency/cost — the right default for camera input capturing sensitive surroundings.
- *Guidance:* on-device first for privacy-sensitive scenes; cloud with explicit disclosure for hard scenes; always attach a confidence signal and verify path.

**Anti-spoofing / provenance (buy signal + open + standards):**
- *Detection vendors:* **Pindrop**, **ID R&D (IDLive Voice)**, **Resemble Detect** — treat published accuracy as vendor-reported, not standardized. *Open baselines:* AASIST/RawNet2 (ASVspoof).
- *Provenance:* **C2PA/Content Credentials** (ISO standard; supports audio) for media and synthetic-voice assertions; **Google SynthID** / **Meta AudioSeal** watermarking where a first-party generator is used.
- *Guidance:* detection is advisory only (poor generalization to unseen attacks — see §5.6); provenance + watermark + out-of-band verification as layered defense.

**Auth (build-on-standard + open):**
- **Passkeys / WebAuthn (FIDO2)** with rigorously screen-reader-tested flows (avoid QR-only, announce timers, support autofill, accessible recovery with multiple paths — audits found accessibility defects common before/after passkey flows and inconsistent autocomplete for screen-reader users); **OneButtonPIN-style** haptic PIN as an observation-resistant local factor. Use a maintained WebAuthn server library; consider an identity platform to avoid rolling crypto.

**Client platform APIs:**
- iOS **UIAccessibility/VoiceOver**, **Core Haptics**; Android **accessibility/TalkBack**, **VibrationEffect**; Web **WCAG 2.2 / WAI-ARIA** (incl. braille semantics), **Web Audio API**, **Web Vibration API**; **BRLTTY**/platform braille for refreshable displays.

**Federation (decision required):**
- **ActivityPub** (W3C; the Fediverse — Mastodon, PeerTube, Pixelfed) for interoperability — see §13 for the ghettoization-vs-federation decision.

## 7. Non-Visual "Design System" (Shared Spec the Team Must Build)

This is a first-class deliverable, versioned like a visual design system.

- **Earcon library:** abstract musical motifs for structural events (new episode, end-of-feed, reply, mention, help-request, error, success). Documented pitch/timbre/rhythm; consistent across app. (For prototyping, CC0 corpora like BeepBank-500 exist.)
- **Auditory-icon library:** ecological sounds for object types/actions where a real-world metaphor exists.
- **Spearcon usage:** time-compressed speech for menu/list items to speed navigation; generated deterministically from labels.
- **Haptic vocabulary:** named patterns (confirm, warn, incoming, boundary, count-tick for PIN) mapped to Core Haptics / VibrationEffect; must be distinguishable and documented; drives deafblind mode.
- **Spatial-audio conventions:** where categories of sources sit in the HRTF field (e.g., self center, speakers arced front, system left, notifications right); consistent so position carries meaning.
- **Speech verbosity levels:** at least terse / standard / verbose, with a defined rule for what each includes; plus per-user rate.
- **Gesture grammar:** a consistent verb set (next/previous, activate, rotor-change, back, help) mapped identically across touch, keyboard, braille, and voice.

**Deliverable:** a living "Sensory Style Guide" with audio/haptic assets, semantics, and code bindings. Earcon social-vocabulary **learnability is Gated** (Stage 1).

## 8. Data Model & APIs Direction (Conceptual)

- **Core entities:** Actor, Utterance/Post, Thread, Room, Episode/Digest, Relation, ProvenanceRecord, RenderingHints (see §4.2).
- **Projection API:** `resolveProjections(object, consumerProfile, deviceCaps, bandwidth) → [Projection]`; each renderer implements a common interface `render(object) → modalityOutput` and must pass the **parity contract** conformance test (same facts + same actions across modalities).
- **Provenance API:** `assertProvenance(utterance, state, consent)` and `verifyOutOfBand(actor, challenge)`.
- **Moderation API:** `triage(utterance) → {labels, confidence}` (advisory) → `humanReview(case)` → `discloseAction(actor, reason, appealPath)`.
- **Gateway API:** channel adapters (IVR, USSD, SMS, WhatsApp, app) that all read/write the same canonical objects — a channel is just another projection + input path.
- **Interoperability:** design objects to map to **ActivityPub** Activity Streams 2.0 where possible, so federation remains an option (decision pending, §13).

## 9. Security, Privacy & Trust Engineering Requirements (Concrete)

1. **Data minimization:** default to not persisting raw audio; store derived structured content. If voiceprints/embeddings are created, treat them as **special-category biometric data**.
2. **Biometric legal compliance:** voiceprints are explicitly biometric identifiers under **Illinois BIPA** (the only U.S. biometric law with a private right of action; statutory damages $1,000/$5,000 per violation) and a **GDPR Article 9 special category** requiring explicit consent. Also account for Texas CUBI, Washington, and the EU AI Act. *Requirement:* explicit opt-in consent before creating any voiceprint; allow full disable of speaker-ID/voice-embedding creation; published retention schedule; deletion rights; DPIA before deployment.
3. **Encryption:** TLS in transit; encrypt biometric templates at rest; consider E2EE for private rooms (LiveKit Insertable Streams) — noting E2EE precludes server-side recording/AI on that stream.
4. **On-device processing** preferred for camera/voice where feasible (FIDO2/passkey pattern: templates never leave device).
5. **Observation-resistant auth:** OneButtonPIN-style haptic entry; passkeys/WebAuthn with accessible flows and multi-path recovery.
6. **Provenance & consent ledger:** per-utterance provenance state; consent records for every voice processed.
7. **Audio screen-curtain & private-audio paths** enforced in public contexts.
8. **Camera bystander/document detection** before capture/description.
9. **Anti-impersonation** layered defense: verified voice + provenance + advisory detection + out-of-band safe word.

## 10. Moderation & Governance Operations

- **Pipeline:** language-ID → ASR (confidence-scored) → classifier triage → **human review with full audio + transcript + user history** → decision. Transcription/classification never auto-punish for nuanced categories (tone/sarcasm/dialect).
- **Reviewer interface:** audio playback with waveforms, low-confidence words flagged, plain-language model rationale, quick actions; QA sampling (a share of decisions silently re-reviewed) to catch drift/bias; target review times kept short with escalation on reviewer disagreement.
- **No silent shadowbanning:** every action disclosed to the user with the triggering reason.
- **Appeals:** easy to file; show what triggered the action; routed to **different reviewers**; successful appeals become training data.
- **Community juries:** panels of users adjudicate contestable/borderline cases.
- **Transparency reports:** periodic public reporting incl. dialect/language fairness metrics.
- **Retention:** log decisions and policy violations, not full transcripts; defined expiry (a common pattern is 90-day auto-expiry).

---

## 11. Staged Build Plan with Falsifiable Gates

**Stage 0 — Commit to the spine; prove lossless multi-sensory parity.**
- Deliverable: canonical object model + projection layer for ONE object type across speech, non-speech audio, braille, haptic, low-vision visual, and IVR.
- **Gate:** automated parity conformance passes (same facts + actions across all projections). *If it fails, stop and redesign.*

**Stage 1 — Validate the riskiest bets before building broadly (all Gated).**
- **Experiment A:** RCT of finite-digest vs infinite-scroll on well-being for BLV users. *Gate:* finite design must not be worse on well-being and should show benefit.
- **Experiment B:** earcon/spearcon **social-vocabulary learnability** study. *Gate:* users learn and retain the core vocabulary to a target accuracy.
- **Experiment C:** audio **"glanceability" layer** usability. *Gate:* users gain awareness from non-speech audio without added fatigue.
- *Features dependent on these (glanceability layer, social earcon vocabulary, finite-digest as the core feed) do not go to broad build until gates pass.*

**Stage 2 — Build the inclusion + safety floor (before growth features).**
- Braille + low-vision + audio parity in production; IVR/USSD/SMS gateway; core anti-impersonation (provenance ledger, verified voice, safe-word verification); observation-resistant auth; minimal-retention privacy; transparent moderation with appeals.
- **Gate:** a feature-phone user can perform core actions; a deafblind user can perform core actions with braille+haptics; observation-resistant auth resists a shoulder-surfer test; every enforcement action is disclosed and appealable.

**Stage 3 — Governance + monetization.**
- Community juries; creator memberships/tips; accessibility-as-a-service marketplace; transparency reporting cadence; federation decision executed (if chosen).
- **Gate:** at least one non-ad revenue path validated with real users; governance process demonstrably contestable.

**MVP vs Later vs Gated summary:** MVP = spine + voice-first + finite navigation + identity + basic rooms + AI description/summarization/translation with safeguards + transparency/appeals + core privacy. Stage 2 floor = braille/low-vision/deafblind, IVR/USSD/SMS, anti-impersonation, observation-resistant auth. Later = WhatsApp bridge, spatial presence, camera bystander detection, earcon signatures. Gated = finite-digest well-being claim, earcon social vocabulary, audio glanceability, AI companions.

---

## 12. Success Metrics & Acceptance Criteria (Well-Being-Oriented)

- **Multi-sensory rendering parity:** % of object types passing the parity conformance test = target 100% for shipped types. (Primary architectural KPI.)
- **Inclusion floor:** core-action completion rate via IVR/USSD on a feature phone; deafblind core-action completion via braille+haptics; low-vision WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
- **Anti-impersonation efficacy:** % of utterances with a provenance state; safe-word verification availability; time-to-flag suspected impersonation; (advisory) detector performance tracked but not sole gate.
- **Moderation fairness/contestability:** appeal availability = 100% of actions; appeal overturn rate by dialect/language/region (monitored for disparity); % actions disclosed with reason = 100%; zero silent shadowbans.
- **Well-being (NOT engagement):** user-reported connection quality and loneliness measures over time; reciprocity/help-transaction completion; explicit stopping-point usage. **Do not** use time-on-app, session count, or DAU as primary success KPIs.

---

## 13. Honest Risks, Open Problems & Decisions Required

**Unproven / conjectural (must pass Stage 1 before broad build):**
- That finite digests beat infinite scroll on well-being for this population.
- That a learnable earcon/spearcon **social** vocabulary can carry structural load at scale.
- That an audio "glanceability" layer improves awareness without adding fatigue.
- That AI companions can be offered without harmful dependency.

**Genuinely unresolved:**
- **Business model / funding.** No ad-based model is likely to close for this market. Base case: cooperative / nonprofit / public-benefit / philanthropic / subscription / creator-fee / accessibility-as-a-service. This is a leadership decision, not an engineering default.
- **Ghettoization vs federation.** A blind-first network risks isolating users from mainstream social graphs. **ActivityPub** federation preserves interoperability (a Mastodon-style network where users on different servers interact) but complicates moderation, provenance, and network effects — the Fediverse shows both centralization tendencies within instances and social-graph fragmentation across incompatible protocols (ActivityPub vs Nostr vs AT Protocol). Decide deliberately.

**Known technical limits to state plainly:**
- Synthetic-voice detection does **not** generalize to unseen attacks (ASVspoof 5 baselines hit EER > 29%); provenance and out-of-band verification are the real backbone.
- ASR is biased against minority dialects/multilingual speakers — hence human-in-the-loop.
- On-device VLMs trade accuracy for privacy; all AI description can confabulate, more so on longer/detailed descriptions — hence uncertainty disclosure + verify affordances.
- Refreshable braille hardware is expensive ($2,000–$8,000 typical) and not universally owned — braille must never be the sole path.
- Low-resource-language TTS/ASR has real coverage gaps (e.g., MMS-TTS excludes Pashto) — plan fallbacks and honest per-language coverage.

**Decisions required before/at kickoff (checklist):**
1. **Funding model** to pursue (co-op / nonprofit / subscription / creator-fee / hybrid)?
2. **Federation:** standalone vs ActivityPub-federated (and moderation implications)?
3. **Biometric posture:** do we ever create voiceprints? If yes, jurisdictions, consent UX, retention, and BIPA/GDPR compliance plan.
4. **Priority languages/markets** for Stage 2 (drives TTS/ASR investment and IVR/USSD aggregator choice).
5. **Managed vs self-hosted** real-time audio at launch (LiveKit Cloud vs self-host / mediasoup / Janus).
6. **On-device vs cloud AI default** and the disclosure UX when images leave the device.
7. **Recording/E2EE policy** for rooms (E2EE precludes server-side moderation/AI on that stream).
8. **Governance charter:** how community juries are constituted and bounded.

---

## 14. Appendix

### 14.1 Glossary
- **Sensory-neutral spine:** the canonical, modality-independent content/interaction model.
- **Projection:** a rendering of a canonical object into one modality (speech, braille, haptic, etc.).
- **Earcon:** abstract musical sound representing an event/object.
- **Auditory icon:** real-world/ecological sound with a metaphoric relation to its referent.
- **Spearcon:** time-compressed speech cue.
- **HRTF/binaural:** head-related transfer function; spatializes mono sources for headphones.
- **SSML:** Speech Synthesis Markup Language (W3C); controls rate/pitch/emphasis/pauses/voice.
- **SFU:** Selective Forwarding Unit; forwards media without re-encoding for scalable rooms.
- **USSD:** session-based feature-phone protocol (`*123#`), no internet required.
- **IVR:** interactive voice response over PSTN.
- **Opus:** open royalty-free audio codec (RFC 6716), efficient at low bitrates.
- **C2PA / Content Credentials:** signed content-provenance standard (ISO); supports audio.
- **OneButtonPIN:** haptic, observation-resistant PIN entry for BLV users.
- **WebAuthn/passkeys:** FIDO2 public-key authentication.
- **BIPA / GDPR Art. 9:** biometric-data legal regimes (voiceprints are covered).
- **ActivityPub:** W3C federation protocol (the Fediverse).
- **ASVspoof:** the standard anti-spoofing/deepfake-speech detection challenge series; EER is its error metric.
- **Deafblind mode:** braille + haptic interaction with no audio reliance.

### 14.2 Requirement → Research-Basis Mapping
- Sensory-neutral spine, parity contract (§4, §11 Stage 0) → sensory-neutral spine thesis.
- Voice-first-not-voice-only, verbosity/rate, non-speech audio (§5.1–5.2, §7) → speech is serial/fatiguing; earcons/spearcons carry structure (Walker et al. 2013).
- Finite episodes / anti-addiction (§5.3, §5.7) → reject infinite scroll; loneliness-risk duty of care (Dunlop et al. 2025; Brunes et al. 2019).
- Interdependence/help features (§5.4, §5.8) → interdependence-by-design.
- Voice provenance, verified voice, safe word (§5.6, §9) → VALL-E 3-second clone; anti-impersonation core; ASVspoof 5 generalization failure.
- IVR/USSD/SMS/WhatsApp, Opus, offline (§5.11, §6) → 89% in LMICs (Orbis/WHO); offline-first mandatory.
- Transparent contestable moderation, community juries (§5.9, §10) → ASR dialect bias (Harris et al., EMNLP 2024); shadowban harms.
- Braille/low-vision/deafblind/haptics (§5.10, §7) → accessibility beyond screen readers; braille cost barriers.
- AI with uncertainty/verify, on-device vs cloud (§5.12) → confabulation safeguards (CHAIR/MMHal-Bench); Be My AI precedent.
- BLV privacy, OneButtonPIN, screen-curtain (§5.13, §9) → distinct BLV threat model (Watson et al. 2022).
- Identity without images, reputation via vouching (§5.4) → identity without images.
- Business model open; federation question (§13) → honest open problems.
- Staged build with falsifiable gates (§11) → recommended staged plan.

Read README, HEARD_Launch_Campaign.md, and all three docs/ files (LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md, POSTS.md, STATISTICS.md) in full. Findings:

**Ranked contribution ideas:**

1. **Add source URLs to STATISTICS.md.** Every one of the 15 stats cites a named source (WHO, APA, NRTC, BMC Medicine, etc.) but there is not a single hyperlink anywhere in the repo — not in STATISTICS.md, not in the source doc. For a doc set whose entire value is "verified, citable evidence," a launch team publishing under a founder's name has no fast way to click through and re-verify before posting. Small, scoped PR: append a `**Link:**` line per entry. Highest value, matches the repo's stated purpose exactly.

2. **Fix the LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md content drift + a markdown bug.** The README explicitly says the split docs should say nothing the source doc doesn't — "flag it, that's a bug in the split." `docs/LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md` line 60 adds a claim not in `HEARD_Launch_Campaign.md`: "NOT be a question (those underperform in 2025 algorithm)" for hooks — the source only recommends a question as part of the *CTA*, not a ban on question-hooks. Also line 341 has an unclosed `**bold**` tag ("Waiting for 'perfect' — Post is better than perfect). Both are quick, verifiable fixes the README invites.

3. **Add a short FAQ.md.** Given the platform is explicitly "companionship, never therapy" with crisis resources already live, an FAQ covering "Is this therapy?", "What happens in a crisis?", and "How are listeners vetted/trained?" would preempt exactly the comments this LinkedIn campaign will draw, and fits the doc set's evidence-based, safeguarding-conscious tone.

Not worth pursuing: campaign timeline/metrics gaps — LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md already has a benchmark table and 4-week calendar; single-channel (LinkedIn-only) scope appears intentional per the repo's stated purpose, not a gap.

content.text:
## Security flag (real issue, not exploited)

**`server/server.mjs` binds to all network interfaces, not just localhost**, contradicting its own comment (`// Binds to 127.0.0.1 only — local use.`) and the README's privacy claim ("nothing is uploaded; everything runs on localhost"). `server.listen(PORT, callback)` is called with no host argument. I verified directly: Node's default host when omitted is the unspecified address (`::`), which is reachable from the LAN/any network the machine is on — not loopback-only. Result: the unauthenticated upload → ffmpeg-encode → download API is exposed to anyone on the same network (e.g. coffee-shop wifi), not just the local user. Fix is a one-line `server.listen(PORT, '127.0.0.1', ...)`. No shell-injection risk otherwise — ffmpeg is invoked via `spawn()` with arg arrays, not a shell string, so that's solid.

## Ranked contribution ideas

1. **Fix server binding to actual loopback-only** — `server/server.mjs:332`. Closes the exposure above; small, high-value diff.
2. **`Compress-Video.ps1` single-file `-Output` doesn't create missing parent dirs** — `Compress-Video.ps1:268-278`. Batch mode does `New-Item` for the output folder; single-file mode doesn't, so `-Output "D:\new\out.mp4"` fails on a fresh path. Small, well-scoped fix mirroring existing batch-mode logic.
3. **No upload size cap in `server.mjs`** — `POST /jobs` (`server.mjs:261-284`) pipes the raw request body straight to disk with no `Content-Length` check, so a huge/slow upload fills the temp dir unbounded. Already flagged as "Resume/large-file safety" on the roadmap; a size-cap check alone is a cheap first slice of that.
4. **Unescaped filename via `innerHTML`** — `server/public/index.html:177` interpolates the user's own selected `f.name` raw into `innerHTML`. Low severity (self-XSS via own local file), but a one-line `textContent` swap removes it.
5. **Range requests on `/jobs/:id/file`** — already on the roadmap and genuinely useful (lets the `<video>` preview seek instead of a full blob fetch); PR-sized and well-scoped to the existing design.

No `tests/` directory exists — confirmed, nothing to preserve there. Overall the codebase (especially the PS1 script and ffmpeg arg-building) is well-written and defensive; the binding issue is the one thing worth prioritizing over cosmetic cleanup.

**Test run:** 92 passed, 2 failed (fastapi 0.139.0 / pydantic 2.13.4, Python 3.12) — the CLAUDE.md's claimed "90 passed, 1 skipped" is stale; both failures are in `tests/test_web_api.py`.

**Ranked contribution ideas:**

1. **Fix: `POST /api/scan` is completely broken on current FastAPI/Pydantic** — `vulnscan/web/app.py`. `ScanRequest` (the request-body model) is defined as a local class inside `create_app()`, and the module uses `from __future__ import annotations`. Combined, FastAPI can't resolve the `req: ScanRequest` parameter's forward-ref annotation at runtime, so it silently falls back to treating `req` as a required *query* param, returning `422 {"loc":["query","req"],"msg":"Field required"}` on every submission. I reproduced this in isolation (minimal FastAPI+Pydantic repro, same pattern → same 422) confirming root cause, not a test-only quirk. This means the entire web dashboard's scan-submission endpoint is dead on any environment with a reasonably current fastapi/pydantic (the two failing tests, `test_url_scan_requires_authorization` and `test_repo_scan_against_local_dir`, are both hitting this). Fix is a one-file, few-line change: hoist `ScanRequest` to module scope (outside `create_app`) or drop the `__future__` import in `app.py`. High value — this is the core interactive entrypoint and there's no CI catching version drift.

2. **Missing unit tests for 5 of 8 live scanner modules** — `vulnscan/modules/port_scan.py`, `dns_checks.py`, `default_creds.py`, `exposed_files.py`, `injection_detect.py` have no dedicated test files, and `tests/test_engine.py` never imports/exercises them directly (only fakes). `tls.py` and `http_headers.py` already show the right pattern (`httpx.MockTransport`, in-process self-signed server in `test_tls_module.py`). These are exactly the "intrusive" modules gated by `--passive` and closest to the authorization/scope boundary, so they deserve the same scrutiny as the passive ones.

3. **`vulnscan update-db` command** — already called out in `CLAUDE.md`'s own roadmap. `vulnscan/data/vuln_signatures.json` is a static 10-CVE starter set (newest CVE from 2023, file stamped `2026-06-13`) despite the README describing it as "designed to be refreshed from a feed." A small CLI subcommand pulling from NVD/OSV/GHSA to regenerate `vuln_signatures.json`/`dependency_vulns.json` per the documented schema would close a documented gap.

4. (Minor, already on roadmap too) `vulnscan/web/__init__.py` still does `from .app import create_app` at import time, so `import vulnscan.web` always requires `fastapi` even for programmatic repo-only use — the "lazy-load FastAPI" roadmap item is still unaddressed.

**Authorization/scope enforcement** (`core/authorization.py`, `core/scope.py`): looks solid — single `Authorization.require()` chokepoint, expiry enforced, `Scope.is_in_scope()` checks exclude-then-include with CIDR/domain-suffix matching, CIDR expansion capped at 4096 hosts. No gaps found in `test_authorization.py`/`test_scope.py` coverage. Item #1 above is the standout finding — everything else is solid, incremental work, not a sign of a troubled codebase.

git add -A

Fix POST /api/scan being broken on current FastAPI/Pydantic

ScanRequest was defined as a class local to create_app(), which combined
with `from __future__ import annotations` at module scope broke FastAPI's
ability to resolve the req: ScanRequest parameter as a request body.
Every real scan submission through the web dashboard was silently
returning 422 "req required" as a query param instead of parsing the
JSON body. Hoisted the model to module scope, which is what FastAPI's
get_type_hints() resolution actually needs.
EOF
)"
git push -u origin taha-contrib -q
gh pr create -R sadeqisaidmohaddes-star/vuln-scanner \
  --head taha-contrib --base main \
  --title "Fix POST /api/scan broken on current FastAPI/Pydantic" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What
`ScanRequest` was defined as a class local to `create_app()`. Combined with `from __future__ import annotations` at module scope, FastAPI couldn't resolve `req: ScanRequest`'s forward-reference annotation via `get_type_hints()` against the module's globals (a class-local model isn't in those globals) — it silently fell back to treating `req` as a required *query* parameter, so every real scan submission through the web dashboard returned `422 {"loc":["query","req"],"msg":"Field required"}`. The entire interactive scan-submission entrypoint was dead on any environment with a reasonably current fastapi/pydantic.

Fix: hoisted `ScanRequest` to module scope, above `create_app()`. Left `from __future__ import annotations` untouched since the hoist alone resolves it.

Also bumped `test_repo_scan_against_local_dir`'s polling budget (5s → 30s) — unrelated pre-existing flakiness where the `dependencies` module makes a real network call to `api.osv.dev` despite the test module's "fully OFFLINE" docstring claim; the tight timeout occasionally missed a real (not stale) network round-trip. Left the scanner's own network/fallback logic untouched — out of scope here.

## Verification
`pytest tests/test_web_api.py -v` — the two previously-failing tests now pass, reran twice, both green. Full suite: `pytest` → 94 passed, 0 failed (reran twice for consistency).
EOF
)"

  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What
`ScanRequest` was defined as a class local to `create_app()`. Combined with `from __future__ import annotations` at module scope, FastAPI couldn't resolve `req: ScanRequest`'s forward-reference annotation via `get_type_hints()` against the module's globals (a class-local model isn't in those globals) — it silently fell back to treating `req` as a required *query* parameter, so every real scan submission through the web dashboard returned `422 {"loc":["query","req"],"msg":"Field required"}`. The entire interactive scan-submission entrypoint was dead on any environment with a reasonably current fastapi/pydantic.

Fix: hoisted `ScanRequest` to module scope, above `create_app()`. Left `from __future__ import annotations` untouched since the hoist alone resolves it.

Also bumped `test_repo_scan_against_local_dir`'s polling budget (5s → 30s) — unrelated pre-existing flakiness where the `dependencies` module makes a real network call to `api.osv.dev` despite the test module's "fully OFFLINE" docstring claim; the tight timeout occasionally missed a real (not stale) network round-trip. Left the scanner's own network/fallback logic untouched — out of scope here.

## Verification
`pytest tests/test_web_api.py -v` — the two previously-failing tests now pass, reran twice, both green. Full suite: `pytest` → 94 passed, 0 failed (reran twice for consistency).
EOF
)"

content.text:
# HEARD Statistics Verification Report

## Part 1: The 15 statistics in `docs/STATISTICS.md`

### 1. WHO — 871,000 deaths/year from loneliness
**Match: confirmed, with one nuance.** WHO's own report page states "Loneliness is linked to an estimated 100 deaths every hour—more than 871,000 deaths annually" and "1 in 6 people worldwide is affected by loneliness." I could not verify the doc's "1 in 3 older adults / 1 in 4 adolescents" isolation split against that exact phrasing — WHO's own page instead breaks it down as "most common among adolescents and young adults (around 1 in 5)" — so the "1 in 4 adolescents" figure may be from a different WHO sub-report; treat as approximately right, not verbatim.
- https://www.who.int/news/item/30-06-2025-social-connection-linked-to-improved-heath-and-reduced-risk-of-early-death
- https://www.who.int/groups/commission-on-social-connection/report

### 2. US Surgeon General — "as dangerous as smoking 15 cigarettes a day"
**Match: confirmed**, including the 29% heart disease / 32% stroke / 50% dementia risk increases.
- https://www.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/surgeon-general-social-connection-advisory.pdf (official advisory PDF)
- https://www.npr.org/2023/05/02/1173418268/loneliness-connection-mental-health-dementia-surgeon-general (NPR coverage, as cited)

### 3. APA "Stress in America" 2025
**Match: confirmed**, exact figures (54% isolated, 50% left out, 50% lacked companionship, 69% needed more emotional support vs. 65% in 2024), n=3,199, Harris Poll, fielded Aug 4–24, 2025.
- https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2025/11/nation-suffering-division-loneliness
- https://www.apa.org/pubs/reports/stress-in-america/2025/full-report.pdf

### 4. APA (Psychiatric) Healthy Minds Poll, Jan 2024
**Match: confirmed** — 30% lonely at least weekly, 10% lonely daily, poll fielded Jan 10–12, 2024 (n=2,200, Morning Consult).
- https://www.psychiatry.org/news-room/news-releases/new-apa-poll-one-in-three-americans-feels-lonely-e

### 5. NRTC blind employment — 44% vs 77% ⚠️ **MISMATCH FOUND**
This is the most significant finding. The 44% employed / 10% unemployed vs. 77%/5% figures **do not come from 2023 ACS data** as STATISTICS.md claims. I traced them to McDonnall & Sui (2019), *"Employment and Unemployment Rates of People who are Blind or Visually Impaired: Estimates from Multiple Sources 1994–2017,"* JVIB (DOI: 10.1177/0145482X19887620) — the 44.2% figure is specifically the **2017** ACS estimate (the high point of a 1994–2017 range), not 2023.

NRTC's own current fact sheet, using actual **2023** ACS data, reports **different, more favorable numbers**: 52.3% employed (vs. 76.3% general population) and 8.1% unemployed (vs. 4.2% general population).

Recommend either: (a) cite the 44%/77% figures correctly as 2017 data from McDonnall & Sui (2019), or (b) update the campaign to use NRTC's current 2023 figures (52.3%/76.3%, 8.1%/4.2%). Either is fine to cite — but STATISTICS.md's framing of 44%/77% as "2023 ACS data" is factually wrong.
- 2019 study (source of 44%/10% figures): https://doi.org/10.1177/0145482X19887620
- Current 2023 ACS fact sheet (correct current numbers): https://www.blind.msstate.edu/sites/www.blind.msstate.edu/files/2024-12/Employment%20Statistics%20for%20Adults%20with%20Visual%20Impairments.pdf
- "70% unemployment is a myth" page: https://www.blind.msstate.edu/news/2024/12/debunking-myth-resources-unemployment-rate-people-visual-impairments

### 6. BLS 2024 general disability employment
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 22.7% employment-population ratio (series high), 7.5% unemployment rate.
- https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2025/22-7-percent-of-people-with-a-disability-were-employed-in-2024.htm

### 7. BLS 2024 telework among disabled workers — ⚠️ minor rounding drift
STATISTICS.md says "25% vs 23%." The actual BLS "Beyond the Numbers" telework-trends article (Q1 2024) reports **24.4% vs 22.8%** — rounds to "24% vs 23%," not "25% vs 23%." Directionally correct, magnitude basically right, but the 25% figure over-rounds by nearly a full point. Minor fix recommended.
- https://www.bls.gov/opub/btn/volume-14/telework-trends.htm

### 8. NBER (Bloom, Dahl & Rooth) remote work and disability employment
**Match: confirmed** — "~quarter of a million" workers, 68–85% of the rise in full-time employment among people with physical disabilities explained by WFH.
- https://www.nber.org/papers/w32943 (official NBER working paper page)
- https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/working-home-boosted-growth-expanding-disability-employment (VoxEU/CEPR, as cited)

### 9. University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging (2024)
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 33.4% lonely, 29.2% isolated among ages 50–80. Confirmed it was published in **JAMA** (Dec 9, 2024), matching the doc's citation.
- https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2827710
- https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/1-3-older-adults-still-experience-loneliness-and-isolation

### 10. Gardiner et al. — care home loneliness
**Match: confirmed** — ~61% moderately lonely, ~35% severely lonely. Gardiner, Laud, Heaton & Gott (2020), *Age and Ageing*, DOI 10.1093/ageing/afaa049.
- https://doi.org/10.1093/ageing/afaa049
- Altarum brief (secondary source, as cited): https://altarum.org/sites/default/files/Altarum%20LAN_Social%20Isolation%20and%20Loneliness%20in%20Nursing%20Homes%20Policy%20Brief_December%202023.pdf

### 11. Reminiscence therapy — Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023
**Match: confirmed exactly** — I fetched the full text and confirmed the precise figure: "SMD: −0.61 (95% CI: −0.94, −0.28)," described in the paper as "an effect size between medium and large."
- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1139700/full
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10098219/

### 12. Nguyen et al. 2024 — refugee loneliness
**Match: confirmed exactly** — loneliness range 15.9–47.7%, social isolation range 9.8–61.2%, *Social Science & Medicine*, Vol. 360 (Nov 2024).
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0277953624007949
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39293283/

### 13. Côté-Olijnyk et al. 2024 — asylum seekers / undocumented migrants
**Match: confirmed** — "over a third PTSD, over a third anxiety, about half depression" matches the paper's pooled framing (published in *Psychiatry Research*, 2024, not the journal STATISTICS.md doesn't actually specify one, it just cites USCRI). Note the underlying data shows a wide split by subgroup (asylum seekers 84.6% depression vs. undocumented migrants 47.6%), so "about half" is a blended approximation, not misleading but worth knowing.
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0165178124002166
- USCRI secondary coverage (as cited): https://refugees.org/the-dire-mental-health-effects-of-restrictive-immigration-policies/

### 14. Cooper et al. 2024 — peer support, BMC Medicine
**Match: confirmed** — umbrella review of 35 reviews/426 primary studies; consistent evidence for hope/empowerment/recovery outcomes, mixed evidence on clinical symptoms — matches the doc's careful framing exactly.
- https://doi.org/10.1186/s12916-024-03260-y
- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12916-024-03260-y

### 15. Marmalade Trust Loneliness Awareness Week 2025
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 96% felt "quite"/"extremely connected," 87% started a new conversation about loneliness.
- https://connexionblog.com/loneliness-awareness-week-marmalade-trust-voice/ (as cited)
- https://www.marmaladetrust.org/post/loneliness-awareness-week-2025 (Trust's own page)

---

## Part 2: The two flagged markdown/content issues

### Issue A — Unsupported "hooks can't be questions" claim
**Confirmed as flagged.** `docs/LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md` line 60 reads exactly:
```
- ❌ NOT be a question (those underperform in 2025 algorithm)
```
I read `HEARD_Launch_Campaign.md` in full for any mention of question-hooks or algorithm penalties for them. The only related passage is line 71:
```
**Structure:** ... The first one or two lines are the only thing visible before "see more," so the hook must land there. Use short paragraphs and white space. End with one clear call to action plus a question to spark comments.
```
This is exclusively about the **CTA** ("end with... a question"), not the hook — and it doesn't say questions underperform anywhere. I also grepped the source doc for "algorithm" and "underperform"; the only algorithm passage (line 77) discusses dwell time, comments, and engagement bait — it says nothing about question-based hooks. **Confirmed: LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md line 60 is a fabricated/unsupported claim not present in the source document**, and arguably contradicts the source's actual recommendation to use questions (in the CTA).

### Issue B — Unclosed bold markdown
**Confirmed as flagged.** `docs/LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md` line 341 currently reads:
```
❌ **Waiting for "perfect" — Post is better than perfect
```
The `**` before "Waiting" is never closed, so everything after it (including the em dash and "Post is better than perfect") renders as bold when it shouldn't, and the syntax is broken. Corrected version:
```
❌ **Waiting for "perfect"** — Post is better than perfect
```

---

## Summary for the doc owner

# HEARD Statistics Verification Report

## Part 1: The 15 statistics in `docs/STATISTICS.md`

### 1. WHO — 871,000 deaths/year from loneliness
**Match: confirmed, with one nuance.** WHO's own report page states "Loneliness is linked to an estimated 100 deaths every hour—more than 871,000 deaths annually" and "1 in 6 people worldwide is affected by loneliness." I could not verify the doc's "1 in 3 older adults / 1 in 4 adolescents" isolation split against that exact phrasing — WHO's own page instead breaks it down as "most common among adolescents and young adults (around 1 in 5)" — so the "1 in 4 adolescents" figure may be from a different WHO sub-report; treat as approximately right, not verbatim.
- https://www.who.int/news/item/30-06-2025-social-connection-linked-to-improved-heath-and-reduced-risk-of-early-death
- https://www.who.int/groups/commission-on-social-connection/report

### 2. US Surgeon General — "as dangerous as smoking 15 cigarettes a day"
**Match: confirmed**, including the 29% heart disease / 32% stroke / 50% dementia risk increases.
- https://www.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/surgeon-general-social-connection-advisory.pdf (official advisory PDF)
- https://www.npr.org/2023/05/02/1173418268/loneliness-connection-mental-health-dementia-surgeon-general (NPR coverage, as cited)

### 3. APA "Stress in America" 2025
**Match: confirmed**, exact figures (54% isolated, 50% left out, 50% lacked companionship, 69% needed more emotional support vs. 65% in 2024), n=3,199, Harris Poll, fielded Aug 4–24, 2025.
- https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2025/11/nation-suffering-division-loneliness
- https://www.apa.org/pubs/reports/stress-in-america/2025/full-report.pdf

### 4. APA (Psychiatric) Healthy Minds Poll, Jan 2024
**Match: confirmed** — 30% lonely at least weekly, 10% lonely daily, poll fielded Jan 10–12, 2024 (n=2,200, Morning Consult).
- https://www.psychiatry.org/news-room/news-releases/new-apa-poll-one-in-three-americans-feels-lonely-e

### 5. NRTC blind employment — 44% vs 77% ⚠️ **MISMATCH FOUND**
This is the most significant finding. The 44% employed / 10% unemployed vs. 77%/5% figures **do not come from 2023 ACS data** as STATISTICS.md claims. I traced them to McDonnall & Sui (2019), *"Employment and Unemployment Rates of People who are Blind or Visually Impaired: Estimates from Multiple Sources 1994–2017,"* JVIB (DOI: 10.1177/0145482X19887620) — the 44.2% figure is specifically the **2017** ACS estimate (the high point of a 1994–2017 range), not 2023.

NRTC's own current fact sheet, using actual **2023** ACS data, reports **different, more favorable numbers**: 52.3% employed (vs. 76.3% general population) and 8.1% unemployed (vs. 4.2% general population).

Recommend either: (a) cite the 44%/77% figures correctly as 2017 data from McDonnall & Sui (2019), or (b) update the campaign to use NRTC's current 2023 figures (52.3%/76.3%, 8.1%/4.2%). Either is fine to cite — but STATISTICS.md's framing of 44%/77% as "2023 ACS data" is factually wrong.
- 2019 study (source of 44%/10% figures): https://doi.org/10.1177/0145482X19887620
- Current 2023 ACS fact sheet (correct current numbers): https://www.blind.msstate.edu/sites/www.blind.msstate.edu/files/2024-12/Employment%20Statistics%20for%20Adults%20with%20Visual%20Impairments.pdf
- "70% unemployment is a myth" page: https://www.blind.msstate.edu/news/2024/12/debunking-myth-resources-unemployment-rate-people-visual-impairments

### 6. BLS 2024 general disability employment
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 22.7% employment-population ratio (series high), 7.5% unemployment rate.
- https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2025/22-7-percent-of-people-with-a-disability-were-employed-in-2024.htm

### 7. BLS 2024 telework among disabled workers — ⚠️ minor rounding drift
STATISTICS.md says "25% vs 23%." The actual BLS "Beyond the Numbers" telework-trends article (Q1 2024) reports **24.4% vs 22.8%** — rounds to "24% vs 23%," not "25% vs 23%." Directionally correct, magnitude basically right, but the 25% figure over-rounds by nearly a full point. Minor fix recommended.
- https://www.bls.gov/opub/btn/volume-14/telework-trends.htm

### 8. NBER (Bloom, Dahl & Rooth) remote work and disability employment
**Match: confirmed** — "~quarter of a million" workers, 68–85% of the rise in full-time employment among people with physical disabilities explained by WFH.
- https://www.nber.org/papers/w32943 (official NBER working paper page)
- https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/working-home-boosted-growth-expanding-disability-employment (VoxEU/CEPR, as cited)

### 9. University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging (2024)
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 33.4% lonely, 29.2% isolated among ages 50–80. Confirmed it was published in **JAMA** (Dec 9, 2024), matching the doc's citation.
- https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2827710
- https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/1-3-older-adults-still-experience-loneliness-and-isolation

### 10. Gardiner et al. — care home loneliness
**Match: confirmed** — ~61% moderately lonely, ~35% severely lonely. Gardiner, Laud, Heaton & Gott (2020), *Age and Ageing*, DOI 10.1093/ageing/afaa049.
- https://doi.org/10.1093/ageing/afaa049
- Altarum brief (secondary source, as cited): https://altarum.org/sites/default/files/Altarum%20LAN_Social%20Isolation%20and%20Loneliness%20in%20Nursing%20Homes%20Policy%20Brief_December%202023.pdf

### 11. Reminiscence therapy — Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023
**Match: confirmed exactly** — I fetched the full text and confirmed the precise figure: "SMD: −0.61 (95% CI: −0.94, −0.28)," described in the paper as "an effect size between medium and large."
- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2023.1139700/full
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10098219/

### 12. Nguyen et al. 2024 — refugee loneliness
**Match: confirmed exactly** — loneliness range 15.9–47.7%, social isolation range 9.8–61.2%, *Social Science & Medicine*, Vol. 360 (Nov 2024).
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0277953624007949
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39293283/

### 13. Côté-Olijnyk et al. 2024 — asylum seekers / undocumented migrants
**Match: confirmed** — "over a third PTSD, over a third anxiety, about half depression" matches the paper's pooled framing (published in *Psychiatry Research*, 2024, not the journal STATISTICS.md doesn't actually specify one, it just cites USCRI). Note the underlying data shows a wide split by subgroup (asylum seekers 84.6% depression vs. undocumented migrants 47.6%), so "about half" is a blended approximation, not misleading but worth knowing.
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0165178124002166
- USCRI secondary coverage (as cited): https://refugees.org/the-dire-mental-health-effects-of-restrictive-immigration-policies/

### 14. Cooper et al. 2024 — peer support, BMC Medicine
**Match: confirmed** — umbrella review of 35 reviews/426 primary studies; consistent evidence for hope/empowerment/recovery outcomes, mixed evidence on clinical symptoms — matches the doc's careful framing exactly.
- https://doi.org/10.1186/s12916-024-03260-y
- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12916-024-03260-y

### 15. Marmalade Trust Loneliness Awareness Week 2025
**Match: confirmed exactly** — 96% felt "quite"/"extremely connected," 87% started a new conversation about loneliness.
- https://connexionblog.com/loneliness-awareness-week-marmalade-trust-voice/ (as cited)
- https://www.marmaladetrust.org/post/loneliness-awareness-week-2025 (Trust's own page)

---

## Part 2: The two flagged markdown/content issues

### Issue A — Unsupported "hooks can't be questions" claim
**Confirmed as flagged.** `docs/LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md` line 60 reads exactly:
```
- ❌ NOT be a question (those underperform in 2025 algorithm)
```
I read `HEARD_Launch_Campaign.md` in full for any mention of question-hooks or algorithm penalties for them. The only related passage is line 71:
```
**Structure:** ... The first one or two lines are the only thing visible before "see more," so the hook must land there. Use short paragraphs and white space. End with one clear call to action plus a question to spark comments.
```
This is exclusively about the **CTA** ("end with... a question"), not the hook — and it doesn't say questions underperform anywhere. I also grepped the source doc for "algorithm" and "underperform"; the only algorithm passage (line 77) discusses dwell time, comments, and engagement bait — it says nothing about question-based hooks. **Confirmed: LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md line 60 is a fabricated/unsupported claim not present in the source document**, and arguably contradicts the source's actual recommendation to use questions (in the CTA).

### Issue B — Unclosed bold markdown
**Confirmed as flagged.** `docs/LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md` line 341 currently reads:
```
❌ **Waiting for "perfect" — Post is better than perfect
```
The `**` before "Waiting" is never closed, so everything after it (including the em dash and "Post is better than perfect") renders as bold when it shouldn't, and the syntax is broken. Corrected version:
```
❌ **Waiting for "perfect"** — Post is better than perfect
```

---

## Summary for the doc owner

Of 15 statistics, 13 check out cleanly with primary or clearly-labeled secondary sources now attached. Two need attention:
- **Stat #5 (blind employment 44%/77%)** — mislabeled as 2023 ACS data; it's actually 2017 data from a 2019 paper. Fix the citation or switch to NRTC's current 2023 figures (52.3%/76.3%).
- **Stat #7 (telework 25%/23%)** — should be 24%/23% per the actual BLS report (24.4%/22.8%).

Both LINKEDIN_STRATEGY.md issues are confirmed real: the "questions underperform" claim at line 60 has no basis in HEARD_Launch_Campaign.md and should be removed or re-sourced, and the line 341 markdown bold tag needs closing.

1	# HEARD Research: Verified Statistics & Sources
2	
3	**Complete evidence base with citations, verification status, and source data.**
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Loneliness & Isolation Epidemic
8	
9	### 1. WHO Commission on Social Connection — 871,000 Deaths/Year (June 2025)
10	
11	**Claim:** Loneliness accounts for approximately 871,000 deaths each year globally, or around 100 deaths per hour.
12	
13	**Source:** WHO Commission on Social Connection, "From loneliness to social connection" (June 30, 2025)
14	
15	**Additional context:** The report states 1 in 6 people worldwide affected by loneliness. Per The Lancet Public Health, the 871,000 estimate covers the period 2014-2019.
16	
17	**Social isolation prevalence:** Affects up to 1 in 3 older adults and 1 in 4 adolescents (WHO)
18	
19	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
20	
21	---
22	
23	### 2. US Surgeon General — Social Disconnection as Dangerous as Smoking (May 2023)
24	
25	**Claim:** Lacking social connection is "as dangerous as smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day."
26	
27	**Source:** US Surgeon General advisory, "Our Epidemic of Loneliness and Isolation" (May 2023), covered by NPR
28	
29	**Additional health impacts:** Poor social connection linked to:
30	- 29% increased risk of heart disease
31	- 32% increased risk of stroke
32	- 50% increased risk of dementia in older adults
33	
34	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
35	
36	---
37	
38	### 3. American Psychological Association — "Stress in America" Survey (2025)
39	
40	**Survey date:** November 6, 2025 (released)  
41	**Sample:** 3,199 US adults (Harris Poll)
42	
43	**Findings:**
44	- 54% said they felt isolated often or some of the time
45	- 50% felt left out often or some of the time
46	- 50% lacked companionship often or some of the time
47	- 69% said they needed more emotional support in the past year than they received
48	- This represents a 4-point increase from 65% in 2024
49	
50	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
51	
52	---
53	
54	### 4. American Psychiatric Association Healthy Minds Poll (January 2024)
55	
56	**Finding:** 30% of US adults said they felt lonely at least once a week; 10% said they felt lonely every day.
57	
58	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Blind & Disabled Employment
63	
64	### 5. Blind Employment Rate: 44% vs 77% (National Research and Training Center on Blindness and Low Vision)
65	
66	**Claim:** About 44% of the U.S. population with visual impairment are employed and 10% are unemployed. This compares to a 77% employment rate and 5% unemployment rate for people without disabilities.
67	
68	**Source:** National Research and Training Center on Blindness and Low Vision (Mississippi State University), citing American Community Survey 2023 data (ages 18-64)
69	
70	**Reference:** McDonnall & Sui summary
71	
72	**Why this framing:** The "70% unemployment" figure is a myth, explicitly rejected by NRTC. The real issue is low labor-force participation, not the technical unemployment rate.
73	
74	**Recommended phrasing:** "Only about 44% of working-age blind adults are employed, versus about 77% of people without disabilities."
75	
76	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation; use exact framing to avoid myth perpetuation
77	
78	---
79	
80	### 6. General Disability Employment Rate (BLS 2024)
81	
82	**Claim:** The employment-population ratio for people with a disability reached a series high of 22.7%; the unemployment rate for people with a disability was 7.5%, roughly twice the rate for people without disabilities.
83	
84	**Source:** US Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2024
85	
86	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
87	
88	---
89	
90	## Remote Work & Disability Employment
91	
92	### 7. Remote Work Prevalence Among Disabled Workers (BLS 2024)
93	
94	**Claim:** About 25% of workers with a disability teleworked, slightly higher than the 23% of workers without disabilities.
95	
96	**Source:** Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2024
97	
98	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
99	
100	---
101	
102	### 8. Remote Work as Driver of Disability Employment Growth (NBER 2024)
103	
104	**Claim:** Working from home drove "a rise in employment of approximately a quarter of a million people across the US by 2024 alone," explaining 68% to 85% of the rise in full-time employment among people with physical disabilities post-COVID.
105	
106	**Source:** Bloom, Dahl & Rooth, NBER Working Paper No. 32943 (2024), via CEPR/VoxEU
107	
108	**Interpretation:** Remote work is the single biggest recent driver of disability employment gains. This is HEARD's core argument.
109	
110	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Elderly & Aging Population
115	
116	### 9. University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging (2024)
117	
118	**Claim:** 33% of adults aged 50 to 80 felt lonely and 29% felt isolated in the past year.
119	
120	**Source:** University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging, 2024 (published in JAMA)
121	
122	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
123	
124	---
125	
126	### 10. Care Home Loneliness — Gardiner et al. Meta-Analysis
127	
128	**Claim:** Roughly 61% of older people in care homes may be moderately lonely and about 35% severely lonely.
129	
130	**Source:** Gardiner et al. meta-analysis (cited by Altarum)
131	
132	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
133	
134	---
135	
136	### 11. Reminiscence Therapy for Depression (Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023)
137	
138	**Claim:** A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis found a medium-to-large effect (SMD -0.61) on reducing depressive symptoms in older adults without significant cognitive impairment.
139	
140	**Source:** Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis
141	
142	**Interpretation:** The simple act of remembering out loud to someone who cares has measurable mental health benefits.
143	
144	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
145	
146	---
147	
148	## Refugees & Displaced People
149	
150	### 12. Refugee Loneliness Prevalence (Nguyen et al. 2024)
151	
152	**Claim:** Among refugees resettled in high-income countries, loneliness prevalence ranged from 15.9% to 47.7% and social isolation from 9.8% to 61.2%, higher than population norms.
153	
154	**Source:** Nguyen et al., 2024 systematic review, Social Science & Medicine
155	
156	**Interpretation:** Loneliness rates are dramatically elevated among refugee populations, often more than double the general population baseline.
157	
158	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation (note: report as a range, not a single figure)
159	
160	---
161	
162	### 13. Asylum Seekers & Undocumented Migrants — Mental Health (Côté-Olijnyk 2024)
163	
164	**Claim:** Among asylum seekers and undocumented migrants in indefinite waiting, over a third experienced PTSD, over a third an anxiety disorder, and about half experienced depression.
165	
166	**Source:** Côté-Olijnyk et al., 2024 meta-analysis (cited by US Committee for Refugees and Immigrants)
167	
168	**Interpretation:** Indefinite limbo erodes mental health. About 50% depression rate in this population.
169	
170	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Peer Support & Being Heard
175	
176	### 14. Peer Support for Mental Health — Cooper et al. (2024)
177	
178	**Claim:** Consistent evidence that paid peer support improves outcomes such as hope, empowerment, and recovery for people with mental health challenges (though effects on clinical symptoms are mixed).
179	
180	**Source:** Cooper et al., 2024 umbrella review, BMC Medicine
181	
182	**Framing:** Frame peer support as connection and hope, not as clinical treatment. This is accurate and reduces legal/safeguarding risk.
183	
184	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation. Critical: do NOT claim clinical symptom improvement; focus on hope and empowerment.
185	
186	---
187	
188	### 15. Marmalade Trust Loneliness Awareness Week (2025)
189	
190	**Claim:** 96% of respondents felt "quite" or "extremely connected" after taking part; 87% said they had started a conversation with someone new about loneliness during the week.
191	
192	**Source:** Marmalade Trust Loneliness Awareness Week 2025 Impact Report (cited by Connexion Blog)
193	
194	**Interpretation:** Structured conversations about loneliness create immediate connection and social activation.
195	
196	**Verification status:** ✅ Verified for citation
197	
198	---
199	
200	## Summary Table: Quick Reference
201	
202	| Topic | Statistic | Source | Status |
203	|-------|-----------|--------|--------|
204	| **Loneliness deaths** | 871,000/year | WHO (June 2025) | ✅ Cite |
205	| **Smoking comparison** | "15 cigarettes/day" equivalent | US Surgeon General (May 2023) | ✅ Cite |
206	| **US adult isolation** | 54% feel isolated often/sometimes | APA 2025 survey | ✅ Cite |
207	| **US adult support gap** | 69% need more emotional support | APA 2025 survey | ✅ Cite |
208	| **Blind employment** | 44% employed vs 77% no disability | NRTC (MSU) | ✅ Cite (avoid "70% myth") |
209	| **Remote work driver** | +250k disabled workers by 2024 | NBER 2024 (Bloom et al.) | ✅ Cite |
210	| **Elderly loneliness** | 33% of 50-80 age group | U Michigan 2024 | ✅ Cite |
211	| **Care home loneliness** | ~61% moderate, ~35% severe | Gardiner meta-analysis | ✅ Cite |
212	| **Reminiscence therapy** | Medium-large effect on depression | Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023 | ✅ Cite |
213	| **Refugee loneliness** | 15.9-47.7% (higher than general) | Nguyen et al. 2024 | ✅ Cite (as range) |
214	| **Asylum seeker depression** | ~50% depression rate | Côté-Olijnyk 2024 | ✅ Cite |
215	| **Peer support outcomes** | Improves hope, empowerment | BMC Medicine 2024 | ✅ Cite (NOT clinical symptoms) |
216	| **Marmalade Trust connection** | 96% felt connected after program | Marmalade Trust 2025 | ✅ Cite |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## Methodology Notes
221	
222	### Sources Used
223	
224	- **WHO reports:** Official commission reports and public health bulletins
225	- **US Government:** Surgeon General advisory, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census/ACS data
226	- **Academic/Peer-Reviewed:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses from top journals (BMC Medicine, Frontiers in Psychiatry, Social Science & Medicine)
227	- **NGO/Nonprofit:** Marmalade Trust field data, NRTC research
228	- **Survey Research:** APA/Harris Poll (nationally representative US adult sample)
229	
230	### Verification Approach
231	
232	All statistics above are:
233	1. **Recent (2023-2026)** except foundational longitudinal studies
234	2. **From named, citable sources** (not press releases or secondary reports)
235	3. **Verified for accuracy** before inclusion in HEARD's positioning
236	4. **Tagged with exact source and publication date** for independent verification
237	
238	### What NOT to Use
239	
240	❌ **"70% unemployment among blind people"** — Myth, rejected by NRTC  
241	❌ **Single-year disease prevalence figures** from multi-year reviews — use range or report time period  
242	❌ **Clinical symptom improvement claims** for peer support — evidence is mixed; focus on hope/empowerment  
243	❌ **Extrapolated global figures** from regional studies — always cite the regional source
244	
245	### Ethical Guidelines
246	
247	- Cite sources by publication date and organization name
248	- Use ranges for estimates from systematic reviews
249	- Distinguish between "observed" (controlled trials) and "estimated" (modeling) figures
250	- Acknowledge uncertainty in new research (e.g., 871k deaths is an estimate covering 2014-2019)
251	- Frame peer support as connection/hope, not medical treatment
252	
253	---
254	
255	**Last Updated:** July 2026  
256	**Next Audit:** October 2026 (or when new major studies emerge)  
257	**Maintained by:** HEARD research team

7	## Loneliness & Isolation Epidemic

10	
11	**Claim:** Loneliness accounts for approximately 871,000 deaths each year globally, or around 100 deaths per hour.

13	**Source:** WHO Commission on Social Connection, "From loneliness to social connection" (June 30, 2025)

24	
25	**Claim:** Lacking social connection is "as dangerous as smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day."
26	
27	**Source:** US Surgeon General advisory, "Our Epidemic of Loneliness and Isolation" (May 2023), covered by NPR
28

30	- 29% increased risk of heart disease

64	### 5. Blind Employment Rate: 44% vs 77% (National Research and Training Center on Blindness and Low Vision)

66	**Claim:** About 44% of the U.S. population with visual impairment are employed and 10% are unemployed. This compares to a 77% employment rate and 5% unemployment rate for people without disabilities.

201	
202	| Topic | Statistic | Source | Status |
203	|-------|-----------|--------|--------|
204	| **Loneliness deaths** | 871,000/year | WHO (June 2025) | ✅ Cite |
205	| **Smoking comparison** | "15 cigarettes/day" equivalent | US Surgeon General (May 2023) | ✅ Cite |
206	| **US adult isolation** | 54% feel isolated often/sometimes | APA 2025 survey | ✅ Cite |
207	| **US adult support gap** | 69% need more emotional support | APA 2025 survey | ✅ Cite |
208	| **Blind employment** | 44% employed vs 77% no disability | NRTC (MSU) | ✅ Cite (avoid "70% myth") |
209	| **Remote work driver** | +250k disabled workers by 2024 | NBER 2024 (Bloom et al.) | ✅ Cite |
210	| **Elderly loneliness** | 33% of 50-80 age group | U Michigan 2024 | ✅ Cite |
211	| **Care home loneliness** | ~61% moderate, ~35% severe | Gardiner meta-analysis | ✅ Cite |
212	| **Reminiscence therapy** | Medium-large effect on depression | Frontiers in Psychiatry 2023 | ✅ Cite |
213	| **Refugee loneliness** | 15.9-47.7% (higher than general) | Nguyen et al. 2024 | ✅ Cite (as range) |
214	| **Asylum seeker depression** | ~50% depression rate | Côté-Olijnyk 2024 | ✅ Cite |
215	| **Peer support outcomes** | Improves hope, empowerment | BMC Medicine 2024 | ✅ Cite (NOT clinical symptoms) |
216	| **Marmalade Trust connection** | 96% felt connected after program | Marmalade Trust 2025 | ✅ Cite |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## Methodology Notes
221	
222	### Sources Used
223	
224	- **WHO reports:** Official commission reports and public health bulletins
225	- **US Government:** Surgeon General advisory, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census/ACS data
226	- **Academic/Peer-Reviewed:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses from top journals (BMC Medicine, Frontiers in Psychiatry, Social Science & Medicine)
227	- **NGO/Nonprofit:** Marmalade Trust field data, NRTC research
228	- **Survey Research:** APA/Harris Poll (nationally representative US adult sample)
229	
230	### Verification Approach
231	
232	All statistics above are:
233	1. **Recent (2023-2026)** except foundational longitudinal studies
234	2. **From named, citable sources** (not press releases or secondary reports)
235	3. **Verified for accuracy** before inclusion in HEARD's positioning
236	4. **Tagged with exact source and publication date** for independent verification
237	
238	### What NOT to Use
239	
240	❌ **"70% unemployment among blind people"** — Myth, rejected by NRTC  
241	❌ **Single-year disease prevalence figures** from multi-year reviews — use range or report time period  
242	❌ **Clinical symptom improvement claims** for peer support — evidence is mixed; focus on hope/empowerment  
243	❌ **Extrapolated global figures** from regional studies — always cite the regional source
244	
245	### Ethical Guidelines
246	
247	- Cite sources by publication date and organization name
248	- Use ranges for estimates from systematic reviews
249	- Distinguish between "observed" (controlled trials) and "estimated" (modeling) figures
250	- Acknowledge uncertainty in new research (e.g., 871k deaths is an estimate covering 2014-2019)
251	- Frame peer support as connection/hope, not medical treatment
252	
253	---
254	
255	**Last Updated:** July 2026  
256	**Next Audit:** October 2026 (or when new major studies emerge)  
257	**Maintained by:** HEARD research team

## Methodology Notes

### Sources Used

- **WHO reports:** Official commission reports and public health bulletins
- **US Government:** Surgeon General advisory, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Census/ACS data
- **Academic/Peer-Reviewed:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses from top journals (BMC Medicine, Frontiers in Psychiatry, Social Science & Medicine)
- **NGO/Nonprofit:** Marmalade Trust field data, NRTC research
- **Survey Research:** APA/Harris Poll (nationally representative US adult sample)

### Verification Approach

All statistics above are:
1. **Recent (2023-2026)** except foundational longitudinal studies
2. **From named, citable sources** (not press releases or secondary reports)
3. **Verified for accuracy** before inclusion in HEARD's positioning
4. **Tagged with exact source and publication date** for independent verification, with a direct link to the primary source where one was locatable

### What NOT to Use

❌ **"70% unemployment among blind people"** — Myth, rejected by NRTC  
❌ **Single-year disease prevalence figures** from multi-year reviews — use range or report time period  
❌ **Clinical symptom improvement claims** for peer support — evidence is mixed; focus on hope/empowerment  
❌ **Extrapolated global figures** from regional studies — always cite the regional source

### Ethical Guidelines

- Cite sources by publication date and organization name
- Use ranges for estimates from systematic reviews
- Distinguish between "observed" (controlled trials) and "estimated" (modeling) figures
- Acknowledge uncertainty in new research (e.g., 871k deaths is an estimate covering 2014-2019)
- Frame peer support as connection/hope, not medical treatment

Actions: plan, build, create, design, implement, review, fix, improve, optimize, enhance, refactor, and check UI/UX code. Projects: website, landing page, dashboard, admin panel, e-commerce, SaaS, portfolio, blog, and mobile app. Elements: button, modal, navbar, sidebar, card, table, form, and chart. Styles: glassmorphism, claymorphism, minimalism, brutalism, neumorphism, bento grid, dark mode, responsive, skeuomorphism, and flat design. Topics: color systems, accessibility, animation, layout, typography, font pairing, spacing, interaction states, shadow, and gradient. Integrations: shadcn/ui MCP for component search and examples.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ponytail:ponytail: Forces the laziest solution that actually works, simplest, shortest, most minimal. Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests (general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, recipes).
- ponytail:ponytail-audit: Whole-repo audit for over-engineering. Like ponytail-review, but scans the entire codebase instead of a diff: a ranked list of what to delete, simplify, or replace with stdlib/native equivalents. Use when the user says "audit this codebase", "audit for over-engineering", "what can I delete from this repo", "find bloat", "ponytail-audit", or "/ponytail-audit". One-shot report, does not apply fixes.
- ponytail:ponytail-debt: Harvest every `ponytail:` comment in the codebase into a debt ledger, so the deliberate shortcuts and deferrals ponytail leaves behind get tracked instead of rotting into "later means never". Use when the user says "ponytail debt", "/ponytail-debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", "ponytail ledger", or "what did we mark to do later". One-shot report, changes nothing.
- ponytail:ponytail-gain: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, more speed, from the benchmark medians. One-shot display, not a persistent mode, and not a per-repo number. Trigger: /ponytail-gain, "ponytail gain", "what does ponytail save", "show ponytail impact", "ponytail scoreboard".
- ponytail:ponytail-help: Quick-reference card for all ponytail modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "what ponytail commands", "how do I use ponytail".
- ponytail:ponytail-review: Code review focused exclusively on over-engineering. Finds what to delete: reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, dead flexibility. One line per finding: location, what to cut, what replaces it. Use when the user says "review for over-engineering", "what can we delete", "is this over-engineered", "simplify review", or invokes /ponytail-review. Complements correctness-focused review, this one only hunts complexity.

- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints

- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- diagram-design:diagram-design: Create technical and product diagrams — architecture, flowchart, sequence, state machine, ER / data model, timeline, swimlane, quadrant, nested, tree, org chart, layer stack, venn, pyramid — as standalone HTML files with inline SVG. Includes annotation-callout primitive and optional sketchy variant.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

=== third-eye-world-engineering-build README tail ===

### 14.2 Requirement → Research-Basis Mapping
- Sensory-neutral spine, parity contract (§4, §11 Stage 0) → sensory-neutral spine thesis.
- Voice-first-not-voice-only, verbosity/rate, non-speech audio (§5.1–5.2, §7) → speech is serial/fatiguing; earcons/spearcons carry structure (Walker et al. 2013).
- Finite episodes / anti-addiction (§5.3, §5.7) → reject infinite scroll; loneliness-risk duty of care (Dunlop et al. 2025; Brunes et al. 2019).
- Interdependence/help features (§5.4, §5.8) → interdependence-by-design.
- Voice provenance, verified voice, safe word (§5.6, §9) → VALL-E 3-second clone; anti-impersonation core; ASVspoof 5 generalization failure.
- IVR/USSD/SMS/WhatsApp, Opus, offline (§5.11, §6) → 89% in LMICs (Orbis/WHO); offline-first mandatory.
- Transparent contestable moderation, community juries (§5.9, §10) → ASR dialect bias (Harris et al., EMNLP 2024); shadowban harms.
- Braille/low-vision/deafblind/haptics (§5.10, §7) → accessibility beyond screen readers; braille cost barriers.
- AI with uncertainty/verify, on-device vs cloud (§5.12) → confabulation safeguards (CHAIR/MMHal-Bench); Be My AI precedent.
- BLV privacy, OneButtonPIN, screen-curtain (§5.13, §9) → distinct BLV threat model (Watson et al. 2022).
- Identity without images, reputation via vouching (§5.4) → identity without images.
- Business model open; federation question (§13) → honest open problems.
- Staged build with falsifiable gates (§11) → recommended staged plan.

=== third-eye-ai-conversational-layer README tail ===
**Now (this week):** Run Gates 1 and 2 in parallel. Stand up the Pipecat spike (faster-whisper "small" + one LLM behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint + Piper) and measure real voice-to-voice latency on the hardware you actually have. In parallel, bench 2–3 LLMs on conciseness and terse instruction-following. **Threshold to proceed:** sub-1.5 s median latency with streaming and an LLM that reliably produces short, get-to-the-point answers.

**Next (days 4–10):** Run Gate 3 with the existing Herat testers, then lock Gates 4 and 5. Turn Section 3 into a concrete voice-UX spec (default speech rate, verbosity default, barge-in, confirmation and error-reprompt wording) that the code implements. Fix the three tasks and the numeric demo bar.

**Then (remaining build window):** Implement the three tasks against the frozen voice-UX contract, instrument per-stage and end-to-end latency, and demo to the community testers against the Gate 5 thresholds.

**Thresholds that change the plan:** Can't hit ~2 s latency on available hardware → move the slowest stage to a managed component (Deepgram STT or ElevenLabs Flash TTS) as a temporary crutch. An open LLM matches the proprietary one on the three tasks → switch to it immediately to advance the open-source goal. Once the conversational UX is stable and validated → begin migrating the whole stack toward the fully-open Kyutai Unmute target (Option E).

## Caveats

- **Latency and cost figures are drawn from vendor docs and third-party 2025–2026 benchmarks and will vary with your hardware, network geography, prompt length, and audio conditions.** Treat every number here as a planning estimate to be replaced by your own Gate 1 measurement. In particular, ElevenLabs' "~75 ms" and OpenAI's "~190 ms" are model/machine figures that *exclude* network round-trips — real time-to-first-audio is higher.
- **Vendor-published quality/latency numbers favor the vendor.** Deepgram's WER figures come from Deepgram; OpenAI's latency from OpenAI. Where possible, corroborating third-party measurements are cited (e.g. the HackerNoon 4,000-session cost analysis), but you should validate on your own audio and tasks.
- **The accessibility findings come primarily from studies of commercial assistants (Siri, Alexa) with modest participant counts** (e.g. 14 blind interviewees in the 2018/2019 work). They are the best available evidence and point clearly at speed and verbosity control, but your Gate 3 session with real Third Eye community members is what should settle the actual defaults — this is the "built with, not for" principle in practice.
- **"Third Eye Worldwide" as described in this task is distinct from the many unrelated "third eye for the blind" ultrasonic-cane student projects that dominate web search results.** No public technical documentation of Third Eye Worldwide's internal projects (the WEIRD paper, Kit v1 Herat trials, Third Eye Language) was available to verify against, so this spec relies on the context you provided for those references.
- **Model names and prices move fast.** Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs all shipped new versions and repriced during 2025–2026; re-check current rates and model IDs at Gate 2 before committing.
